around.headline: Karnataka farmer loses Rs 1.9 lakh after his phone goes missing during a bus journey
around.summary: A Karnataka farmer lost Rs 1.9 lakh after his phone went missing on a bus and was used to access his bank accounts, per today's report. If your phone goes missing while travelling, call your bank to block UPI/net-banking access immediately rather than waiting till you're home.

around.headline: Man who stole chains from women seated near train windows arrested in Bengaluru
around.summary: Police have arrested a man who targeted women seated near train windows to snatch their gold chains, according to today's report. If you're seated near a window with visible jewellery, especially when the train is stopped, keep chains tucked in and stay alert to anyone lingering just outside.

around.headline: Autorickshaw drivers skipping meters for inflated "booster" fares across Bengaluru
around.summary: Autorickshaw fares are reportedly climbing as drivers increasingly skip the meter for negotiated "booster" rates, per today's report. Booking through an app so the fare is fixed upfront is a simpler fix than negotiating on the street.

around.headline: Bengaluru Metro hit by 15 technical-glitch disruptions in the past 10 months
around.summary: Bengaluru Metro has faced 15 service disruptions from technical glitches over the last 10 months, according to today's report. If your commute depends on a tight Metro connection, keep a backup route in mind since these glitches have been recurring rather than one-off.

around.headline: State cabinet renews push to suspend scam-hit KPSC chief
around.summary: The state cabinet is renewing its push to suspend the Karnataka Public Service Commission chief over a scam, per today's report. Worth watching if you or family are preparing for state exams under the commission, as leadership turmoil can affect exam schedules.

around.headline: Cognizant notifies individuals of a data breach, offers $1 million identity-theft cover
around.summary: Cognizant has notified affected individuals of a data breach and is offering $1 million in identity-theft cover, per today's report. If you've worked with or been a client of Cognizant, be wary of calls or emails citing the breach to sound credible — never share OTPs or personal details even if the caller seems to know real details.

around.headline: UK forecasters warn the coming El Nino could be the most intense in over a century
around.summary: UK forecasters say the upcoming El Nino pattern could be the strongest in over a century, according to today's report. For Bengaluru, that raises the odds of an erratic monsoon this year — worth factoring less predictable rain into outdoor plans over the coming months.

street_smart.title: Someone messages you off a classifieds app wanting to rent your car for 12 hours, cash upfront, no rental-app booking — like today's Bengaluru case where a self-drive rental car vanished after a 12-hour booking and police had to launch a search. What do you do before handing over the keys?
street_smart.based_on: Today's real Bengaluru incident: a rental car vanished after being booked for 12 hours, prompting a police search (The Times of India). Rental traps have appeared in recent briefs from the tenant's side (Aug 7, Aug 10, Aug 20) — this is the first from a vehicle owner's side, so it's a fresh mechanism.
street_smart.situation: The offer is good money for a short rental and he seems friendly and in a hurry, saying he'll pay full cash and return the car by evening.

choices.text: Verify his driving licence and Aadhaar against the originals (not just photos), photograph the car's condition and odometer reading, share a copy of his ID with a family member, and use a written rental agreement with a refundable deposit before handing over the keys.
choices.feedback: Correct — documentation, a deposit, and telling someone else close the exact gap that let today's Bengaluru rental vanish without a trace: without verified ID or an agreement on file, there's very little for police to act on.

choices.text: Skip the paperwork since he seems trustworthy and in a hurry, take the cash, and hand over the keys — you can always call the police if something goes wrong.
choices.feedback: This is the trap: without ID verification, a deposit, or an agreement, police have almost nothing to trace the renter or the vehicle by — exactly the gap fuelling cases like today's.

choices.text: Ask for a photo of his driving licence over WhatsApp before handing over the keys, but skip the in-person verification and deposit.
choices.feedback: A photo alone can be doctored or belong to someone else entirely. Checking the physical original and taking a deposit closes gaps a photo leaves wide open.

choices.text: Insist he use a recognized self-drive rental app instead of a private cash deal — but if he refuses, go ahead anyway since he's offering more money.
choices.feedback: The instinct is right — established platforms have built-in KYC, GPS tracking, and insurance for exactly this scenario — but proceeding after he refuses undoes it. That refusal is itself the biggest red flag.

takeaways: Never hand over your vehicle for a private rental without verifying the renter's original ID (driving licence + Aadhaar) in person, not just a photo.
Always use a written rental agreement with a refundable security deposit — cash-only handshake deals leave you no recourse if the vehicle isn't returned.
For a one-off private rental, prefer an established self-drive platform over a classifieds deal — their KYC, GPS tracking, and insurance exist for exactly this failure mode.

quiz.why: Identity-theft cover of this kind typically bundles credit monitoring, so affected individuals can spot fraudulent accounts opened in their name.

quiz.question: Who was elected as Bangladesh's new President, per today's news?
quiz.why: Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir is the BNP's secretary general, one of Bangladesh's two major political parties alongside the Awami League.

quiz.question: What is the term length of a Rajya Sabha member in India?
quiz.why: One-third of Rajya Sabha members retire every two years, unlike the Lok Sabha which is elected as a whole for a 5-year term.

quiz.question: Which Indian city is historically nicknamed the "Manchester of India" for its textile industry?
quiz.why: Ahmedabad earned the name in the 19th century when it became a major hub of cotton textile mills, much like Manchester in England.
